unresolvedMajorIssues: Horizontal gutters and the desktop shell position change from screen to screen, so the app does not read as one layout system
The workout screen shows fewer exercises per phone viewport than the baseline did

findings.evidence: On mobile the left gutter is about 16px on Today, Import error, Prompts and Library. It is about 28px on Routine detail and Workspace, about 42px on Import paste, about 44px on Routines and History, and about 56px on the Builder. Import paste and Import error are the same route but their content starts at different x positions. On desktop the sidebar sits at x≈28 on Prompts, x≈234 on Workout and x≈361 on Routines and History. Prompts content spans about 990px, while Routines and History are about 300px wide in the middle of an otherwise empty canvas. The sidebar also keeps a hamburger toggle inside the persistent nav.
findings.userConsequence: Moving between screens makes the page frame jump sideways and change width. Content sits against different edges on different pages, which looks unfinished. On desktop it is unclear what the layout is. Routines and History have large empty bands on both sides, while Prompts runs a preset field nearly 930px wide.
findings.suggestedChange: Use one mobile gutter, 16px or 20px, on every route. Use one desktop shell with a fixed sidebar position and a shared content max-width, with prose and form fields capped to a readable measure. Remove the redundant hamburger from the persistent desktop sidebar or give it a clear purpose.

findings.evidence: Each exercise card now spends a full row on the labeled tools History / Edit / Replace / Unit lb. The prescription, prescribed note, set row and note/rest row each sit on their own line. The first phone viewport shows the Warm-up card in full and only the top of Squat, whose set chips are cut off behind the sticky footer. The baseline phone capture showed three exercises. In the mobile captures the Squat rest timer and 'Start' control are not visible.
findings.userConsequence: The labels are clearer, but the logging screen takes more scrolling per exercise. During a set the user sees roughly one card instead of two or three. The sticky bar covers chips with no fade or edge, so they read as clipped.
findings.suggestedChange: Keep the text labels but put History as the main tool beside the exercise name. Move Edit, Replace and Unit into a labeled 'More' menu, or lay the tools out in a single compact row. Put the set chips and timer on one line. Add a top fade or padding above the sticky bar so rows scroll under it cleanly.

findings.evidence: Resolve shows '0 of 1 handled' with a disabled-looking 'Review import →'. Confirm then shows '4 exercises mapped to catalog' in green, 'Squat needs a specific version chosen.' under Review notes, and an unqualified dark 'Save program' button. The screens do not say whether saving with Squat unresolved is allowed or what happens to its history link. This matches an objection from the baseline Sol review (R00-SOL-06) and the implementation response does not address it.
findings.userConsequence: A user cannot tell whether the import is ready or is about to save an ambiguous mapping. The green success line and the unresolved note contradict each other.
findings.suggestedChange: Say which exercises are mapped and which are not, for example '3 mapped · 1 needs a version'. State what saving does with unresolved names, for example 'Squat will be saved without linked history'. Give the 'Review' button next to the note the main emphasis until resolved.

findings.evidence: The JSON textarea in Import paste and Import error is about 64px tall and shows two and a half lines of a long routine. The rest of the screen is blank. In Builder, 'Save routine' is the strongest control on a Day 1 with 'Strength 0 ex', and about 60% of the viewport is empty. The implementation response keeps this behavior on purpose because an empty day may be a rest day.
findings.userConsequence: The user cannot check what was pasted before validating. The builder gives no cue that a day with nothing in it will be saved as it is.
findings.suggestedChange: Make the textarea taller and grow it with its content, or show a line count under it. In the builder, label an empty section as 'Empty — will save as rest day', or warn before saving a routine in which every day is empty.

findings.evidence: The captures cut off at 'Appearance / Theme', so the theme control cannot be seen. The reported fix for the dark Workspace theme selection cannot be checked from the frozen image. The destructive 'Import workspace · Replace all local data — destructive' row is now outlined in orange, which is the same colour used for the storage and persistence warnings. The 'Storage usage' label wraps to two lines beside its value.
findings.userConsequence: This round's evidence does not show that the dark theme selection is fixed. The restore row looks like another warning, not like the one action that overwrites data.
findings.suggestedChange: Reorder or crop the Workspace capture so the Theme control is visible in both themes. Mark the restore row with a distinct danger treatment (red text or a separate 'Danger zone' group) and leave amber for advisory warnings.

findings.evidence: The desktop History capture shows 'Dumbbell Shoulder Press' with a darker highlight that reads as a selected row, though the surrounding rows do not. Desktop History still says 'Tap a movement to see every version and session.' The sort row reads 'sort · Sessions Name Recent', with the bullet marking the active option and no visible selected state. The filter chips 'all / recent / stale' have no explanation. Desktop Prompts keeps a 930px-wide preset name field and an unconstrained 'Name this preset…' row.
findings.userConsequence: A leftover hover or focus state looks like a selection. Mouse users are told to 'tap'. A new user cannot tell what 'stale' means or which sort is active.
findings.suggestedChange: Don't capture a hover state, or style hover and selection differently. Use 'Select a movement' on desktop. Show the active sort as a filled segmented control. Define 'stale' with a small hint, or rename it.

findings.evidence: Exercise history still shows 'VOL 2,025' with no unit (this matches baseline Sol finding R00-SOL-08). Version labels such as 'BARBELL SQUAT' are in very small monospace caps. The heatmap labels (M, W, F, S) and the profile card headings 'Body' and 'Training history' are about 11px or smaller, and the 'Body' card has extra empty space above its title. The green dot next to each day on Routine detail is not explained. Routine map cards (the 12 day tiles) have no chevron or other sign that they are tappable.
findings.userConsequence: Small, unlabeled details still make the numbers and status marks harder to read. The user may not know that the volume is in pounds, what the dot means, or that the map tiles open a day.
findings.suggestedChange: Add a unit to VOL, for example 'lb'. Raise the smallest labels to at least 12px. Add a short status label or a legend for the dot. Give map tiles a chevron or hover state.

findings.evidence: Every mobile screen repeats its title twice: the top-bar label on the right ('Today', 'Routines', 'Workout', 'Prompts') and the page heading below it. The top bar's right-hand label is light gray and small. Today step 1 is an outlined card with a dark button, while steps 2 and 3 use plain text links, so the three steps look unequal. Session summary hides the sticky bar behind the sheet, which is cleaner than baseline.
findings.userConsequence: The duplicate label uses space and adds noise without extra orientation. Steps 2 and 3 look like footnotes next to step 1, even though they are the next actions once step 1 is done.
findings.suggestedChange: Drop the right-hand top-bar label, or use it for contextual actions only. Give steps 2 and 3 the same button treatment (secondary) as the current-step button, and keep the primary treatment for whichever step is current.

strengths: The Prompts screen now puts one 'Copy prompt · 5,501 chars' primary button and a 'Go to Import' secondary button at the top, with coach text collapsed. This fixes the baseline objection from all three reviewers.
Today onboarding has numbered steps, a clear current-step action ('Go to Profile →') and a 'Build a routine manually' alternative.

Routine detail leads with 'Start workout', a one-line analysis summary with a 'View analysis' link, week tabs and a day list with 'View day' buttons. This is a clear improvement over the baseline analysis card.
Routines now has a page title, counts, 'New routine' and an 'Open' button on each row. Storage filenames and the 'OTHER' label are gone.
Page titles now follow one large-heading pattern on most screens, including Workspace, and the desktop sidebar adds persistent navigation.
Import errors show a bordered alert with 'Copy recovery prompt for your AI chat' as the main action. The file input is styled as a button.
History export puts Copy first, shows a populated preview with sessions/entries/sets counts, and does not imply an in-app AI.
Profile charts now have dates and starting and current values, and the heatmap has start and end dates.
Library chips wrap instead of being cut off, and the dark and light themes keep the same structure.
The session summary sheet is concise, hides the sticky bar behind it, and offers 'Review session' and 'Next day →'.
limitations: Review used only the 27 frozen static screenshots; I did not run or interact with the app, and I did not read any other current-round output.
Contrast is judged by eye. I measured no ratios, and the implementation response's token measurements are not independently verified here.
Dark theme is evidenced by four captures and desktop by four. Parity for the other screens, and responsive behavior outside 390×844 and 1280×900, is not shown.
Long pages (Profile, Prompts, Library, Workspace, Import confirm) were captured above the fold only, so the Theme control and content below are not reviewed.
Screenshots cannot show keyboard, screen-reader, touch-target, persistence or focus behavior. Pixel offsets and sizes above are visual estimates from the images.
Some baseline comparisons (workout density, desktop shell) were made against the baseline screenshots I opened; the other baseline screens were not re-opened except through the prior findings.

findings.evidence: The desktop shell changes position substantially between routes. Prompts places the sidebar at the left edge and begins content around x256. Routines and History place the sidebar around x360 and compress the content into roughly 300 pixels. Workout uses another position and an intermediate content width. History retains phone-width controls despite the large empty canvas.
findings.userConsequence: Navigation and page titles move when changing destinations. History stays cramped while Prompts stretches controls across nearly the entire remaining window, weakening the sense of one coherent desktop app.
findings.suggestedChange: Keep the desktop sidebar and content origin fixed across routes. Apply route-specific maximum widths inside that stable shell, and give History enough width for a comfortable list.

findings.evidence: On mobile, navigation, workout metadata, Format guide, and the bodyweight card occupy the area above the first exercise, which starts around y322. The warmup card then occupies about 250 pixels. The main-lift set fields are cut by the fixed footer in the captured viewport, and the accessory is entirely below it. Desktop also shows only the accessory heading and tool row above the footer.
findings.userConsequence: The labels are understandable, but routine logging requires substantial scrolling between exercises. Administrative controls and repeated tools consume space needed for the actual sets.
findings.suggestedChange: Reduce the space before the first exercise and compress repeated card chrome. Consider moving occasional Edit and Replace actions into a labeled menu while keeping History and set logging immediately available. Preserve the readable prescription and set sizes.

findings.evidence: Resolve exercises explicitly offers choosing a version or keeping a custom name, and its Review import button appears disabled at 0 of 1 handled. However, Confirm import still says '4 exercises mapped to catalog' alongside 'Squat needs a specific version chosen' and an enabled Save program button. This is the unresolved confirmation objection from the prior Sol review.
findings.userConsequence: The confirmation does not explain whether saving will retain a custom exercise, preserve an ambiguous mapping, or require a later correction.
findings.suggestedChange: Make the confirmation describe the actual saved result. Distinguish mapped exercises from custom or unresolved exercises, and state explicitly whether the remaining review note is optional.

findings.evidence: Session headers still show compact, letter-spaced labels such as 'VOL 2,025' without a unit. Version names such as BARBELL SQUAT are also rendered in very small uppercase text. This retains part of the previous history-label objection.
findings.userConsequence: Users cannot tell what the volume figure measures, and distinguishing exercise versions requires closer reading than the set values themselves.
findings.suggestedChange: Use a plain label such as 'Volume 2,025 lb' if that matches the calculation, or explain the calculation when it cannot be represented by a single unit. Increase the version-label size and reduce letter spacing.

findings.evidence: The builder shows a Strength section with '0 ex' while Save routine is the strongest action. Nothing visible explains whether this is a valid rest day, an incomplete training day, or a routine that can be saved for later editing.
findings.userConsequence: A new user cannot confidently predict what saving this empty training day produces. The implementation response acknowledges the ambiguity but the interface does not resolve it.
findings.suggestedChange: Keep valid empty days supported, but identify their meaning in the UI. Show 'Rest day' when intentional, or explain that the routine can be saved unfinished and edited later.

findings.evidence: Each week repeats three small dots, and each day ends with a green dot. The dots have no visible legend or status label. In the dark capture, the unselected week dots are particularly subdued. The analysis summary also presents 'B 89' and 'partial' without explaining the scale or what is incomplete in the collapsed view.
findings.userConsequence: The explicit Start workout and View day actions are clear, but the supporting status and analysis symbols still require interpretation.
findings.suggestedChange: Replace redundant dots with concise status text or provide one visible legend. Give the analysis summary a readable description such as '89/100 · partial assessment' if those meanings are accurate.

findings.evidence: The pasted routine is visible through a textarea only about three lines high despite substantial unused space below. The export preview is larger, but the long metadata preamble consumes almost all of the visible preview before workout records begin.
findings.userConsequence: Users can perform the copy/paste workflow, but inspecting the supplied routine or checking the useful part of an export requires scrolling inside small text areas.
findings.suggestedChange: Give pasted JSON a larger default editing area. For export, summarize scope and counts outside the preview and make the first workout record visible sooner while preserving the complete exported text.

strengths: Every frozen manifest image was opened directly and was readable.
Today presents explicit setup actions and a clear manual-builder alternative.
Both Prompts captures expose Copy prompt immediately, explain the external AI workflow, and keep preset saving secondary.
Workout tools have understandable visible labels, and prescriptions and entered set values are easy to distinguish.
Routine overview gives Start workout clear priority and keeps detailed analysis collapsed.
Import error recovery has a clear alert and a prominent action for returning to the external AI conversation.
Library filters wrap visibly, and category counts are readable in both supplied themes.
Workspace clearly prioritizes backup, distinguishes destructive restoration, and explains browser-local data risks.
Profile charts now show useful dates, bodyweight values, and a training-frequency time range.
The session summary gives concise completion feedback and clear next actions.
Primary actions and ordinary text are visually legible across the supplied light and dark captures.
limitations: Reviewed exactly the 27 candidate images. No source inspection, live interaction, app mutation, file edits, installation, commits, pushes, or delegation was performed.
Prior findings, the baseline assessment, and the implementation response were read. Baseline images were not opened, so no direct screenshot-to-screenshot regression is claimed.
The desktop layout inconsistency and workout density are current observations. Their regression status is not established.
The visible Workspace captures end before the theme selector, so they cannot confirm the reported selected-theme fix.
Static captures cannot prove keyboard behavior, accessible names, touch target bounds, persistence, data safety, sticky behavior while scrolling, or offscreen recovery paths.
Contrast judgments are visual observations, not measured ratios or accessibility conformance claims.
No other current-round reviewer output or parent conversation was consulted.

unresolvedMajorIssues: Desktop shell width and sidebar position shift between routes in the frozen 1280px captures; most desktop content collapses to phone-width columns.

findings.evidence: The persistent sidebar is at the far left in Prompts, about 220 pixels in in Workout, and about 350 pixels in in Routines and History at the same 1280px viewport. The content columns are roughly 990, 555, and 305 pixels wide. This is a regression from the baseline's stable centered desktop column.
findings.userConsequence: Desktop users cannot build a stable spatial model of the app: the navigation and content move every time they switch screens, Routines and History collapse to a phone-width strip with most of the canvas empty, and the desktop shell reads as broken rather than persistent.
findings.suggestedChange: Anchor the sidebar and content to one shared frame with a viewport-width grid and a single content max-width, then recapture all four desktop routes at 1280px to confirm the navigation does not move.

findings.evidence: The top card shows a green '4 exercises mapped to catalog'. The next card, Review notes, says 'Squat needs a specific version chosen.' with an enabled Review button, while the sticky footer still offers an enabled primary Save program.
findings.userConsequence: A user cannot tell whether Squat is mapped, will be kept as a custom exercise, or still needs a decision. They may save while assuming a catalog link exists and lose history linkage for that exercise.
findings.suggestedChange: State the actual outcome in the note, for example 'Squat will be saved as a custom exercise', and make the green line reflect only catalog-mapped entries; or block Save until the note is resolved.

findings.evidence: The Routine JSON textarea is only about two and a half lines tall and clips the pasted object mid-string, while more than half of the 844px screen below is empty. There is no line or character count and no expand affordance, and the file row still leaves native 'No file chosen' text beside the styled Choose File button.
findings.userConsequence: The user cannot verify what they pasted before validating, and the principal import input feels like an afterthought despite available space; a clipped-looking paste can prompt unnecessary re-pasting or distrust.
findings.suggestedChange: Let the textarea grow to show roughly 8-12 lines or auto-expand, show a character or line count and a short expected-shape hint, and make the file chooser a secondary control that displays the selected filename.

findings.evidence: The new labeled History, Edit, Replace and Unit actions are a clear improvement. 'Unit lb' still reads as static text rather than a toggle and does not show the alternate unit; 'Set rest' is a dotted-underlined phrase with no visible duration or timer action. The set chips and Add set control are clear.
findings.userConsequence: A user can miss that lb can switch to kg, or fail to set the rest duration, leaving two guess points during the principal logging task.
findings.suggestedChange: Use a small segmented lb/kg control or a labeled select for the unit, and show the rest duration and timer affordance together, for example 'Rest 2:00' with a clock and play control, instead of a dotted label.

findings.evidence: History's sort row reads 'sort · Sessions Name Recent'; 'Sessions' and 'Recent' are not self-explanatory, and the active choice is indicated only by an underline. The desktop History still says 'Tap a movement...', and exercise history shows 'VOL 2,025' with no unit.
findings.userConsequence: Users cannot predict the ordering, desktop users see phone-only wording, and volume values cannot be interpreted without guessing the unit.
findings.suggestedChange: Use explicit labels such as 'Most sessions', 'Name', and 'Most recent' inside a clearly interactive sort control, change 'Tap' to 'Select' at desktop widths, and append lb or another unit to VOL.

findings.evidence: Builder's Day 1 shows '0 ex' and only an empty Strength section, yet Save routine is enabled and styled as the primary action with no rest-day explanation. This is the baseline empty-day objection, and the implementation response leaves it open.
findings.userConsequence: A user can save a training day with no exercises without knowing whether that is a valid rest day; if it is not, they discover the problem later when they try to train.
findings.suggestedChange: Either require an exercise before saving, or add an explicit 'Mark as rest day' state and explain what saving an empty day means. Keep the choice behavior-preserving if rest days are valid.

findings.evidence: On mobile the top-right screen name repeats the page h1 immediately below it on Today, Prompts, Routines, History, Library and Workspace. On desktop the persistent sidebar still contains a hamburger that opens a modal drawer duplicating the visible navigation.
findings.userConsequence: Redundant chrome competes with page content and suggests two navigation modes on desktop; it also makes the top-right slot unavailable for a page action.
findings.suggestedChange: Show the top-right label only when it adds context, such as Routines on a routine detail, and hide the sidebar hamburger at desktop widths or repurpose it.

findings.evidence: Profile heatmap weekday labels and streak/average summary, History row metadata, and Library counts use the smallest type in the set. Routine overview puts an unlabeled green dot beside every day while the week tabs use neutral dots and the Routines list labels the routine Not started.
findings.userConsequence: Secondary training data takes effort to read in a gym or at arm's length, and green day dots can be read as completed sessions even though none is shown; the status system is not self-explanatory.
findings.suggestedChange: Set the smallest metadata to a consistent legible size and add a one-word status or legend for the day dots, or remove the green treatment until it means completed.

strengths: Prompts now puts 'Copy prompt · 5,501 chars' and 'Go to Import' at the top in a clear action card; coach prose is collapsed, so the copy and paste AI workflow is obvious.
Today's onboarding gives each step a visible action and a manual builder alternative; the numbered cards read as a sequence rather than inert status rows.
Workout logging is much easier to scan: exercise actions have visible words, prescriptions and set values are larger, the saved 6/6 status is clear, and the Finish workout action is stable.
Routine overview now leads with Start workout and compresses analysis to a grade row with View analysis; the week tabs use Selected and View week labels.
Import recovery and resolution states are explicit: a bordered error alert makes Copy recovery prompt primary, and Review import stays disabled until the exercise is handled.
Light and dark captures share the same structure and section language; color is reinforced with text labels, and the four dark screens remain legible.
History export exposes scope, date range, a summary and a preview with Copy and Download .txt, preserving the offline copy and paste workflow.
Workspace clearly separates backup, destructive workspace import, snapshots and storage-risk language; Profile charts now show dates and axis values.
limitations: Only static screenshots were reviewed; hover, focus, keyboard, screen-reader, persistence, touch and real-device behavior were not tested.
Only 390x844 and 1280x900 were captured; dark evidence covers four screens, and the Workspace theme chips are below the fold, so the reported dark theme-selection fix cannot be verified.
No contrast ratios were measured; color judgments are visual only.

The manifest revision is a2f1717. The repository moved during review: a later commit, 40d6c30, adds width:100% to .app-frame and targets the F1 desktop shift, and the working tree contained further edits. None of that is in the frozen images, so scores judge the 27 supplied captures.
The builder empty-day behavior is treated as an open objection, not proven invalid; no runtime validation was performed.
Actions below the captured fold may exist; findings concern only visible states.
Prior objections still open in the frozen evidence: builder empty-day save (F6), import mapping ambiguity (F2), desktop 'Tap' wording (F5), and unexplained day-dot status (F8).

All 27 manifest images were present and readable; no evidence was missing. Images were opened directly, and source was consulted only after visual review. No current-round reviewer output or parent conversation was consulted.

verificationNote: Focused suites passed, but no complete full-suite pass was established for this historical candidate. Later checks exposed stale Profile wording and the new import count audit marker requirement.
